hypothesis: A drawdown in ROA means the earlier bank gain was reversed into losses.
evidence: 2014 Feb-Jul, 2018 Nov, and 2024 Q3 still show positive total results/ROA flows.
interpretation: A lower positive flow reduces accumulation speed; it does not necessarily subtract from cumulative profit.

hypothesis: The initial overshoot itself explains all cumulative bank profit.
evidence: 2014 Jan is ~35% of Jan-Jul result; Q4-23 is ~45% of Q4-23..Q3-24 diagnostic total.
interpretation: Later periods add positive result through different channels.

hypothesis: Late credit costs erase the earlier accounting result by trough/recovery.
evidence: 2018 cumulative ROA 3.8%a Jan-Nov and 3.9% full-year; 2024 drawdown predates major household mora.
interpretation: Credit costs are real but do not reverse the cumulative sign in measured windows.

hypothesis: A positive cumulative bank result proves the macro shock benefited banks overall.
evidence: No counterfactual isolates profits without shock; normal business and multiple concurrent channels contribute.
interpretation: Accounting sign is not treatment effect.

hypothesis: Nominal 2014/2018 cumulative profits can be compared directly with homogeneous-currency 2023/24.
evidence: Accounting regimes and inflation treatment differ.
interpretation: Compare within episode and direction, not cross-vintage magnitudes.

hypothesis: Monthly annualized ROA can be added or multiplied by current assets to create cumulative pesos.
evidence: Denominators use average assets and annualization; assets vary monthly.
interpretation: Use reported cumulative totals or same-vintage period returns only.
